title: Why does a GTFS route have no departures today?
answer: A route has departures only on dates its trips’ service runs

checks.question: calendar.txt says FULLW runs every day of the week. Why does no trip run on Monday 4 June 2007?
checks.answer: calendar_dates.txt has the row FULLW,20070604,2: exception_type 2 removes FULLW for that one date, overriding the weekly pattern. The other service, WE, runs only on Saturdays and Sundays.

checks.question: Why do the four route 50 trips run on Saturday 9 June but not on Tuesday 5 June?
checks.answer: Their service_id is WE, whose calendar.txt row has 1 only under saturday and sunday.

checks.question: If calendar_dates.txt also had the row FULLW,20070605,2, what would Tuesday 5 June look like?
checks.answer: Like Monday: FULLW would be removed for the day and WE does not run on Tuesdays, so none of the 11 trips would run, though every route stays in routes.txt.

steps.title: On Sunday 3 June 2007, the sample feed runs all 11 trips
steps.line: Predict: which of these bars still run the next day, Monday 4 June 2007?
steps.caption: Google publishes a sample GTFS feed, the CSV files a transit agency gives trip planners, for an invented Demo Transit Authority with 5 bus routes. Here is its day: one bar per trip, labelled with its route and grouped under its service_id, the feed’s name for the timetable a trip follows: FULLW or WE. A trip that runs once spans its first departure to its last arrival; a trip that repeats on a fixed gap spans the hours its vehicles leave the first stop. Grey bars, marked “no service”, do not run that day. On 3 June both timetables run.

steps.title: Monday 4 June 2007 runs none of the 11 trips

steps.picture: Gantt chart: 14 tasks. New in this step: service); service); service); and 11 more.

steps.title: A route has no times; its trips do
steps.line: Follow AB1: route 10’s trip to Bullfrog, service_id FULLW.
steps.caption: routes.txt gives a route its names, vehicle type, colours and web page, and nothing about when it runs. Each row of trips.txt names one route in route_id, so a route has zero or more trips, and names in service_id the timetable the trip follows. A route groups journeys that riders see as one service. It does not itself promise a dated departure. The diagram shows the feed’s tables and the ID columns that join them; the marks at a line’s ends say how many rows can match.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 7 entities, 6 relationships; 10 labels. steps.title: AB1 runs only on the dates its service, FULLW, runs
steps.line: Predict: which rows of the two tables decide Monday 4 June 2007?
steps.caption: A trip’s service_id must match a row of calendar.txt, of calendar_dates.txt, or both. calendar.txt supplies a weekday pattern within a date range; calendar_dates.txt adds or removes a particular date, overriding that pattern. The same service_id can be shared by several trips, so one exception can stop them together without deleting their route. A route has departures only on dates its trips’ service runs: a route row promises nothing by itself. Here FULLW (7 trips) is in calendar.txt and calendar_dates.txt, and WE (4 trips) is in calendar.txt alone.

steps.title: On Monday 4 June 2007, no service runs
steps.line: An exception_type 2 row removes FULLW, overriding the monday column.

Here is its day: one bar per trip, labelled with its route and grouped under its service_id, the feed’s name for the timetable a trip follows: FULLW or WE. A trip that runs once spans its first departure to its last arrival; a trip that repeats on a fixed gap spans the hours its vehicles leave the first stop. Grey bars, marked “no service”, do not run that day. On 8 June only FULLW runs.
steps.picture: Gantt chart: 11 tasks.

steps.title: Saturday 9 June 2007 runs all 11 trips
steps.line: Predict: nothing in routes.txt changed overnight. What decides which trips run?
steps.caption: The date is now 9 June. The route list has not changed, but the active trips have: Four trips under WE start, on route 50. To see why, follow one trip, AB1, from its route to its dates.
steps.picture: Gantt chart: 11 tasks. New in this step: AAMV1, route 50; AAMV2, route 50; AAMV3, route 50; and 1 more.

steps.title: A route has no times; its trips do
steps.line: Follow AB1: route 10’s trip to Bullfrog, service_id FULLW.
steps.caption: routes.txt gives a route its names, vehicle type, colours and web page, and nothing about when it runs. Each row of trips.txt names one route in route_id, so a route has zero or more trips, and names in service_id the timetable the trip follows. A route groups journeys that riders see as one service. It does not itself promise a dated departure. The diagram shows the feed’s tables and the ID columns that join them; the marks at a line’s ends say how many rows can match.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 7 entities, 6 relationships; 10 labels. Marked: ROUTE → TRIP: route_id (each ROUTE has zero or more TRIP, each TRIP has exactly one ROUTE); focused: ROUTE: route_id (id), route_short_name (text); TRIP: trip_id (id), route_id (id), service_id (id); CALENDAR: service_id (id), monday (enum), tuesday (enum), wednesday (enum), thursday (enum), friday (enum), saturday (enum), sunday (enum), start_date (date), end_date (date).

steps.title: AB1 runs only on the dates its service, FULLW, runs
steps.line: Predict: which rows of the two tables decide Saturday 9 June 2007?
steps.caption: A trip’s service_id must match a row of calendar.txt, of calendar_dates.txt, or both. calendar.txt supplies a weekday pattern within a date range; calendar_dates.txt adds or removes a particular date, overriding that pattern. The same service_id can be shared by several trips, so one exception can stop them together without deleting their route. A route has departures only on dates its trips’ service runs: a route row promises nothing by itself. Here FULLW (7 trips) is in calendar.txt and calendar_dates.txt, and WE (4 trips) is in calendar.txt alone.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 7 entities, 6 relationships; 4 labels. Either table: CALENDAR → TRIP: service_id (each CALENDAR has zero or more TRIP, each TRIP has zero or one CALENDAR); CALENDAR_DATE → TRIP: service_id (each CALENDAR_DATE has zero or more TRIP, each TRIP has zero or more CALENDAR_DATE); focused: TRIP: trip_id (id), route_id (id), service_id (id); CALENDAR: service_id (id), monday (enum), tuesday (enum), wednesday (enum), thursday (enum), friday (enum), saturday (enum), sunday (enum), start_date (date), end_date (date); and 1 more. New in this step: 4 labels.

steps.title: On Saturday 9 June 2007, FULLW and WE run
steps.line: The saturday column decides; no exception row matches this date.
steps.caption: Saturday 9 June 2007 lies between start_date and end_date for both services. FULLW has saturday = 1 and runs; WE has saturday = 1 and runs. So all 11 trips run.

steps.title: What leaves a stop: rows of stop_times.txt
steps.line: One row per stop a trip makes, in stop_sequence order.
steps.caption: Which of the running trips leave a given stop? stop_times.txt joins trips to stops: one row for each stop a trip makes, in stop_sequence order, with its times. AB1 leaves Nye County Airport at 8:00 and reaches Bullfrog at 8:10. A trip listed in frequencies.txt repeats through the day on a headway.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 7 entities, 6 relationships; 6 labels. Marked: TRIP → STOP_TIME: trip_id (each TRIP has one or more STOP_TIME, each STOP_TIME has exactly one TRIP); STOP → STOP_TIME: stop_id (each STOP has zero or more STOP_TIME, each STOP_TIME has zero or one STOP); focused: TRIP: trip_id (id), route_id (id), service_id (id); STOP_TIME: trip_id (id), stop_sequence (int), stop_id (id), departure_time (time); and 2 more.

steps.title: Two frequency trips leave Stagecoach Hotel & Casino on 9 June
steps.line: Headways with exact_times empty: the card gives gaps, not times.
steps.caption: A departure is a stop_times row at the stop that is not its trip’s last. CITY1 and STBA start here, on headways with exact_times empty: operators keep the gap, not a timetable. The reference does not say whether a vehicle leaves at end_time, so the card gives gaps. CITY2 ends here and does not count.
steps.picture: “Leaving Stagecoach Hotel & Casino, 9 June”, 7 labelled values.
